title: Hypertension Management 2024–2025: Guideline Updates and Therapeutic Sequencing
summary: Recent European and North American updates converge on earlier initiation of combination therapy, strong use of out-of-office BP, and structured sequencing: ACEi/ARB + CCB or thiazide-like diuretic as the default, with clear roles for β‑blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and device therapy in resistant cases. Targets generally <130/80 mm Hg for most, with some societies retaining <140/90 mm Hg standard targets. Nuanced initiation thresholds for very old adults appear in ESH 2023, whereas ESC 2024 promotes uniform thresholds.
clinicalQuestion: What are the current (2023–2025) evidence-based recommendations for diagnosing, treating, and sequencing pharmacotherapy in adult hypertension, and how do recent guidelines differ?

heroStats.label: Very old (≥80 y) ESH 2023 start
heroStats.value: Often at SBP ≥160 mm Hg; consider 140–160 mm Hg [2]

heroStats.label: First-line classes
heroStats.value: ACEi/ARB, CCB, thiazide-like diuretic; β‑blockers restored role [2], [3]

keyMoments.title: Earlier, combination-first pharmacotherapy
keyMoments.body: ESC 2024 endorses prompt lifestyle + pharmacologic therapy at ≥140/90 mm Hg for all ages, reflecting data that age is not a major effect modifier up to ~85 years. **Single-pill combinations are preferred to accelerate control** [1].

keyMoments.title: ESH nuance for very old adults
keyMoments.body: ESH 2023 permits initiating pharmacotherapy at **SBP ≥160 mm Hg (Class I)** in adults ≥80 years, with consideration at **140–160 mm Hg (Class II)**, and allows a lifestyle-only trial in low-risk grade 1 hypertension before drugs [2], [1].

keyMoments.title: Out-of-office BP emphasized
keyMoments.body: ESH 2023 strongly emphasizes **ambulatory and home BP monitoring** to confirm diagnosis and guide therapy, reducing white-coat and masked hypertension misclassification [4].

keyMoments.title: Therapeutic sequencing clarified
keyMoments.body: Default initial therapy is **ACEi/ARB + CCB or thiazide-like diuretic**; add the third class if needed, then **spironolactone** for resistant hypertension, with **β‑blockers** positioned earlier when compelling indications exist [2], [3].

keyMoments.title: Targets and pragmatism
keyMoments.body: Most modern societies aim for **<130/80 mm Hg** in many adults, while some (e.g., AAFP) recommend a **standard <140/90 mm Hg** target, underscoring shared decision-making and tolerability [5].

sections.title: Confirming Hypertension and Establishing Targets
sections.blurb: Use standardized techniques, confirm with out-of-office readings, and individualize targets based on age, comorbidity, and treatment tolerance.

steps.title: Standardize measurement and confirm with out-of-office BP
steps.body: Use repeat seated office measurements, then confirm with **HBPM or 24-hour ABPM** to exclude white-coat and detect masked hypertension, as emphasized in **ESH 2023** [4], [2].

steps.title: Set initial targets
steps.body: Aim for **<130/80 mm Hg** when tolerated for most non-frail adults per contemporary practice trends; recognize that some groups (e.g., **AAFP**) endorse **<140/90 mm Hg** as a standard target, particularly in primary care contexts [5].

steps.title: Decide when to start medications
steps.body: ESC 2024: **Start drugs at ≥140/90 mm Hg regardless of age/CVD risk** and pair with lifestyle (Class I) [1]. ESH 2023: start at ≥140/90 mm Hg for most, but in **≥80 years**, Class I at **SBP ≥160 mm Hg**, with consideration at **140–160 mm Hg**; low-risk grade 1 may try lifestyle first for several months [2], [1].

sections.title: Stepwise Pharmacotherapy: From First-Line to Resistant Hypertension
sections.blurb: Prioritize combination therapy early, expand to triple therapy, and use mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism before device therapy.

steps.title: Start with 2-drug single-pill therapy
steps.body: Preferred: **ACEi/ARB + DHP-CCB** or **ACEi/ARB + thiazide-like diuretic (chlorthalidone or indapamide)**. **Single-pill combinations improve adherence and speed BP control** [2], [1].

steps.title: Escalate to triple therapy
steps.body: If uncontrolled, add the third class to form **ACEi/ARB + CCB + thiazide-like diuretic** before switching classes [2].

steps.title: Resistant hypertension (≥3 drugs including a diuretic, uncontrolled)
steps.body: Add **spironolactone 12.5–50 mg** as the preferred fourth agent (monitor K+ and renal function). Consider **chlorthalidone/indapamide optimization** and evaluate for secondary causes. For persistent true resistance, consider **renal denervation** in select patients, acknowledging evolving evidence and guideline positioning [2], [6].

steps.title: Role of β‑blockers
steps.body: **β‑blockers are restored as therapeutic options** in ESH 2023, particularly for coronary disease, heart failure with reduced EF, arrhythmias, pregnancy, or sympathetic overactivity; they may be earlier-line in those indications [3], [2].

sections.title: Lifestyle and Adherence Optimization
sections.blurb: Initiate lifestyle measures for all patients at diagnosis and throughout care; they potentiate medications and reduce pill burden.

cards.title: Lifestyle interventions
items: Weight reduction and physical activity; even modest loss lowers BP [7].
DASH-style diet, sodium restriction, and moderation of alcohol [7].
Sleep hygiene and OSA screening when suggestive; treat OSA to aid control.
Smoking cessation and stress reduction to lower overall CVD risk.

cards.title: Adherence and simplification
items: Use **single-pill combinations** when possible to improve persistence [2], [1].
Align dosing with routines; address cost and side effects proactively.
Employ home BP logs and digital reminders; verify technique [4].

sections.title: Tailoring Therapy
sections.blurb: Adjust agents, thresholds, and targets based on comorbidity, age, and physiologic context.

cards.title: Very old adults (≥80 years)
items: **ESC 2024**: treat at ≥140/90 mm Hg similar to younger adults [1].
**ESH 2023**: initiate at **SBP ≥160 mm Hg (Class I)**; consider 140–160 mm Hg based on frailty, orthostasis, and preferences [2].
Prioritize tolerance, orthostatic BP checks, and renal/electrolyte monitoring.

cards.title: Compelling indications
items: CAD, HFrEF, arrhythmias, pregnancy: **β‑blockers** often indicated [3], [2].
CKD/proteinuria: **ACEi/ARB** foundational; diuretic intensity often needed [2].
Diabetes: standard first-line classes; monitor for orthostasis and albuminuria.

cards.title: Emerging/advanced therapies
items: RNA-based therapeutics targeting the renin–angiotensin system (e.g., **AGT knockdown**) show promise for infrequent dosing; **phase II data awaited** [8].
Interventional approaches (e.g., **renal denervation**) are expanding for true resistant cases in specialized centers [6].

sections.title: Follow-Up and Treatment Targets
sections.blurb: Frequency and intensity of follow-up should match risk and BP level.

cards.title: Follow-up cadence
items: Reassess every **4–6 weeks** until control; sooner for stage 2 or high risk.
Use home BP averages to guide titration; confirm control with ABPM when uncertain [4].

cards.title: Targets and de-intensification
items: Aim **<130/80 mm Hg** if tolerated; ensure diastolic not pushed too low in CAD.
AAFP supports a **standard <140/90 mm Hg** target; individualize per frailty and adverse effects [5].
Consider cautious de-intensification if orthostatic symptoms or adverse events emerge.
